## LYME DISEASE AND OTHER TICK-BORNE ILLNESSES
## Inpatient/Outpatient/ER Patients who display signs of illness or fever within 30 days of removing an
attached tick should be evaluated for tick-borne illness. In the upper Midwest
these are Lyme, anaplasmosis, babesiosis, ehrlichiosis, and Powassan virus
disease. Patients who have been bitten by an Ixodes spp. tick (deer tick) but
who do not display signs or symptoms of infection should not be treated with
antimicrobials. Refer to recommendations below for pathogen specific
recommendations.
Anaplasmosis
Ehrlichioisis
Babesiosis
Powassan virus disease - contact Infectious Diseases for more Information.
## Lyme Disease
Lyme disease results from the transmission of Borrelia burgdorferi from an
Ixodes spp. tick bite. Refer to CDC for map of endemic areas.
[CDC Lyme Disease Case Map](orz-gtx-abx-cdc-lyme-disease-case-map)
Prophylactic antimicrobial treatment may be beneficial in certain patients who
have been bitten while in endemic areas.
[Lyme Disease Prophylaxis](orzc-gmenu-lyme-disease-prophylaxis)
Except for [erythema migrans](orzc-gmenu-lyme-erythema-migrans), Lyme disease is a complicated, difficult disease to
diagnose and treat. Infectious Diseases consultation is strongly encouraged.
Refer to recommendations below for
Erythema migrans
[Acute neurological disease](orzc-gmenu-lyme-acute-neuro-disease)
Arthritis
[Cardiac disease](orzc-gmenu-lyme-cardiac-disease)
